<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par44/>''plur.'' by the termination {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}, as in Biblical Aramaic. Nöldeke ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 38 [1884], p. 411) referred doubtfully to the textual readings in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=21|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=15|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=18|verse=12.14.19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, where the Masora uniformly inserts the termination ''û'', and to {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=48|verse=10}} in the Samaritan Pentateuch, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=35}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=13|verse=10}}. In his {{GHGcite|title=Beiträge zur sem. Sprachwiss.}}, p. 19, however, he observes that the construction of a fem. plural with the 3rd sing. fem. is not unexampled, and also that {{GHGheb|text=ה}} is often found as a mistake for {{GHGheb|text=ו}}. On the other hand Mayer Lambert ({{GHGcite|title=Une série de Qeré ketib}}, Paris, 1891, p. 6 ff.) explains all these K<sup>e</sup>thîbh, as well as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=50|verse=6}} (?), and (against Nöldeke) {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=49}} (where {{GHGheb|text=ה}} is undoubtedly the article belonging to the next word), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=16}} (where the {{GHGterm|masc.}} {{GHGheb|text=פָּנַי}} requires the marginal reading), also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=48|verse=41}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=51|verse=56|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=14}}, as remains of the 3rd ''fem. plur.'' in {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}. The form was abandoned as being indistinguishable from the (later) form of the 3rd ''fem. sing.'', but tended to be retained in the perfect of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, as {{GHGheb|text=היה}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} six times in the above examples.

{{GHGmargin-letter|44|n}}
5. The afformatives {{GHGheb|text=תָּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=(תְּ)}}, {{GHGheb|text=תִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=נוּ}} are generally toneless, and the forms with these inflexions are consequently {{GHGterm|Milʿêl}} ({{GHGheb|text=קָטַ֫לְתָּ}}, &c.); with all the other afformatives they are {{GHGterm|Milraʿ}} ({{GHGpar|15|c}}). The place of the tone may, however, be shifted: (''a'') by the {{GHGterm|pause}} ({{GHGpar|29|i}}–v), whenever a vowel which has become vocal Š<sup>e</sup>wâ under the second stem-consonant is restored by the {{GHGterm|pause}}; as {{GHGheb|text=קָטָ֫לָה}} for {{GHGheb|text=קָֽטְלָ֫ה}} ({{GHGheb|text=דָּבֵ֫קָה}} for {{GHGheb|text=דָּֽבְקָ֫ה}}), and {{GHGheb|text=קָטָ֫לוּ}} for {{GHGheb|text=קָֽטְל֫וּ}} ({{GHGheb|text=מָלֵ֫אוּ}} for {{GHGheb|text=מָֽלְא֫וּ}}); (''b'') in certain cases after {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} of the {{GHGterm|Perfect}} (see {{GHGpar|49|h}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|44|o}}
6. Contraction of a final {{GHGheb|text=ת}} with the {{GHGheb|text=ת}} of the afformative occurs e.g. in {{GHGheb|text=כָּרַ֫תִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=2|verse=5}}, &c.; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=20}}, &c., in the ''Perf. Poʿel''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=25}} in the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} of {{GHGheb|text=שׁחת}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=21|verse=2}}, &c., in the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} of {{GHGheb|text=שׁבת}}. Contraction of a final {{GHGheb|text=נ‍}} with the afformative {{GHGheb|text=נוּ}} occurs in {{GHGheb|text=נָתַ֫נּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=16}}; in ''Niph.'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=9|verse=7}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=14|verse=10}}; in ''Hiph.'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=29|verse=19}}; with the afformative {{GHGheb|text=נָה}} in the {{GHGterm|Imperfect Qal}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=17|verse=23}}; {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=71|verse=23}}, where with Baer and Ginsburg {{GHGheb|text=תְּרַנֵּ֫נָּה}} is to be read, according to others {{GHGheb|text=תְּרַנֶּ֫נָּה}} (cf. in ''Polel'' {{GHGheb|text=תְּקוֹנֶ֫נָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=32|verse=16}}), but certainly not {{GHGheb|text=תְּרַנֵּ֫נָה}} with the Mantua ed., Opitius and Hahn; with {{GHGheb|text=נָה}} in the ''Imperat. Hiph.'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=32|verse=9}}.
<section end=par44/>
<section begin=par45/>{{GHGpar-heading|45|The Infinitive}}

F. Prätorius, ‘Ueber den sog. Inf. absol. des Hebr.,’ in {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1902, p. 546 ff.

{{GHGmargin-letter|45|a}}
'''1.''' The Infinitive is represented in Hebrew by two forms, a shorter and a longer; both are, however, strictly speaking, independent ''nouns'' ({{GHGterm|verbal substantives}}). The shorter form, ''the Infinitive construct'' (in Qal {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹל}},<ref>Cf. the analogous forms of the noun, {{GHGpar|93|t}}.</ref> sometimes incorrectly {{GHGheb|text=קְטוֹל}}), is used in very various ways, sometimes in connexion with pronominal suffixes, or governing a substantive in the genitive, or with an accusative of the object (§ 115), sometimes in connexion with prepositions ({{GHGheb|text=לִקְטֹל|translate=to kill}}, {{GHGpar|114|f}}), and sometimes in dependence upon substantives as genitive, or upon verbs as accusative of the object. On the other hand, the use of the longer form, the {{GHGterm|Infinitive absolute}} (in Qal {{GHGheb|text=קָטוֹל}}, sometimes also {{GHGheb|text=קָטֹל}}, obscured from original ''qăṭâl''), is restricted to those cases in which it emphasizes<section end=par45/><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
